title: "cv"
---

Statistician with experience building interpretable models for complex observational data, and the software to fit them at scale. I currently lead the modelling and engineering behind the [Biodiversity Intactness Index (BII)](https://www.nhm.ac.uk/our-science/services/data/biodiversity-intactness-index.html) in the [Biodiversity Futures Lab](https://www.nhm.ac.uk/our-science/research/projects/predicts.html) at the [Natural History Museum](https://www.nhm.ac.uk), London.

I have a PhD in statistics from [the University of Western Australia](https://www.uwa.edu.au/) and was a postdoc at [the University of Cambridge](https://www.cam.ac.uk/), where I developed Bayesian methods for combining mechanistic models with data when those models are known to be wrong.

## Statistical modelling

- **Inference under model misspecification.** Developed the statistical finite element method, a Bayesian framework that embeds a Gaussian process discrepancy term in a mechanistic model so that inference stays honest when the model is wrong.  
  *PNAS*, 2021 · [paper](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2015006118)
- **Scalable Bayesian computation.** Built low-rank approximations and Langevin-based sampling schemes that make posterior inference tractable for high-dimensional models.  
  *J. Comput. Phys.*, 2022 · [paper](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jcp.2022.111261) · *SIAM/ASA JUQ*, 2022 · [paper](DOI)
- **Learning from unstructured data.** Co-developed physics-informed variational autoencoders that link raw, unstructured observations to interpretable latent dynamics.  
  *J. Comput. Phys.*, 2024 · [paper](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jcp.2024.113293)

## Experience

- **Senior Research Software Engineer** — Natural History Museum, London *(2026–present)*
  * Lead the statistical modelling and technical development of the BII, a global biodiversity indicator built on mixed-effects models from over 4 million observations, from over 35 thousand sites from the PREDICTS database.
  * Own the model specification, validation, and uncertainty propagation from site-level data to global projections.
  * Maintain the BII's R packages and HPC/AWS deployment, and work with ecologists to turn research questions into models.
- **Research Software Engineer** — Natural History Museum, London *(2024–2026)*
  * Refactored the BII pipeline into tested R packages and deployed it on HPC.
  * Scaled projections from 10 km to 1 km resolution.
  * Published two CRAN packages (`predictsr`, `ssmooth`) and added CI, testing, documentation, and QA.
- **Postdoctoral Research Associate** — University of Cambridge *(2021–2024)*
  * Recruited to Mark Girolami's group in the final year of my PhD; completed the thesis alongside the first year of the postdoc.
  * Developed Bayesian inference methods (MCMC, Langevin dynamics, filtering) for complex physical models, with a focus on model misspecification and uncertainty quantification.
  * Published in *PNAS*, *SIAM/ASA JUQ*, and the *Journal of Computational Physics*.
- **Teaching Assistant** — University of Western Australia *(2018–2020)*
  * Taught undergraduate and master's statistics courses through tutorials, assessment setting, and exam marking.

## Education

- **PhD in Statistics**, Department of Mathematics and Statistics, University of Western Australia *(2019–2022)*.
  * Thesis: *Statistical finite element methods for nonlinear PDEs*.
- **BSc (Honours)**, Mathematics and Statistics, University of Western Australia *(2015–2018)*.
  * Honours thesis: modelling daily rainfall across Australia with [mixture models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixture_model).

## Skills

**Statistical methods**: hierarchical/mixed-effects models, Bayesian inference and MCMC, mixture models, spatial statistics, uncertainty quantification, model misspecification and model criticism.

**Languages and libraries**:

- **R**: `lme4`, `Stan/brms`, `targets`, `sf`, `terra`, `ggplot2`, `testthat`.
- **Python**: `JAX`, `numpy`, `scipy`, `matplotlib`, `mpi4py`, `pytest`.
- **C++**: `Eigen`, `FEniCS`, `catch2`.

**Tools**: Git, Docker, AWS (EC2/S3), HPC (Slurm, MPI).

## Selected Software

- [**predictsr**](https://github.com/Biodiversity-Futures-Lab/predictsr): an R package to load the [PREDICTS](https://www.nhm.ac.uk/our-science/research/projects/predicts.html) database into R dataframes and cache them to disk. Published on [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/package=predictsr).
- [**ssmooth**](https://github.com/Biodiversity-Futures-Lab/ssmooth): an R package for smoothing spatial data using statistical methods. Published on [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/package=ssmooth).
